method: AI-generated overhead environment artwork animated with a fixed-center vertical camera zoom. Not generative video; depicted terrain/cloud details are reconstructions, not verified observations of exact landing sites.
camera: Strict nadir viewpoint with no horizon or sideways camera motion. Six-second animations from orbit to enlarged surface/cloud detail.

scenes.prompt: Create a new replacement image asset for Hey World, an eight-planet exploration website. Single full-bleed landscape image, 16:9, 2048x1152. STRICT NADIR CAMERA: directly overhead looking vertically down, optical axis perpendicular to the local terrain, authentic map-like aerial photograph. The surface fills EVERY pixel corner-to-corner. No horizon, sky, sun, planet edge or space visible. Photorealistic planetary exploration imaging with restrained natural color, plausible scale, consistent lighting and finely resolved irregular texture; not fantasy concept art, not game render, not glossy or oversharpened. Camera target remains centered for a vertical downward zoom animation. No writing, labels, spacecraft, humans, buildings, roads, borders or watermark. MERCURY: airless heavily cratered rocky regolith in natural low-saturation charcoal and warm gray. Broad older overlapping worn impact craters, a smaller fresh bowl crater just off the exact center, scattered tiny craterlets and rough ejecta, gradual geological variation not evenly repeated polka-dot circles. Hard sun from the upper left creates short consistent shadows INSIDE crater walls; no atmospheric haze or blue cast. View like a high-resolution MESSENGER orbital frame covering a few kilometers. Entire frame is terrain seen straight down, including top edge.
